finding: VM-host enrollment tests ran on Windows although their actual ledger requires POSIX locking and ownership APIs.
cause: StoragePlans._locked deliberately refuses os.name != posix before importing fcntl. The success test expected enrollment; the unsafe-ledger test accidentally accepted this unrelated ValueError as an unsafe-directory refusal.
fix: Keep both enrollment tests POSIX-only; keep the three portable helper cases and the three existing Linux-only /proc tests.
reproducer: probe_windows_fixture_storage_test_suite executes the whole test source with module-local os.name nt and sys.platform win32; the actual native_fixture_storage lock sees the same local os. Global host os/sys/pathlib semantics remain unchanged.
causalAssertion: FixtureStorageTestCapabilityProbeTest executes the preserved source for the exact original unsupported-lock error with three existing Linux skips, then the fixed source for exactly five platform skips and all three portable cases passing.
routineSuite: scripts/check_release_hygiene.sh runs scripts/test_python_platform_contracts.py and scripts/check_python_platform_contracts.py in managed prepush and required CI.
nativeEvidenceLimit: The local probe exercises the recorded platform refusal and test discovery. Actual Windows package CI remains required; the probe neither runs a VM nor claims native storage enrollment acceptance.
